sections.label: Lactation room requirements proposals
sections.summary: Proposes requiring at least one lactation room per 2,500 square metres in offices and business parks, and making lactation room facilities mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, requiring at least one lactation room per 2,500 square metres in gross floor area (GFA) in offices and business parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And second, make certain lactation room facilities mandatory.

sections.label: Breastfeeding prevalence survey finding
sections.summary: HPB said a national survey in 2021 to 2022 showed breastfeeding prevalence was high at 97%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: HPB said a national survey in 2021 to 2022 showed that the prevalence of breastfeeding was high at 97%.

sections.label: Current Code lactation room rule
sections.summary: Currently the Code requires at least one lactation room in offices and business parks of 10,000 square metres or more in GFA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently under the Code, at least one lactation room must be provided in offices and business parks of 10,000 square metres or more in GFA.

sections.label: First proposal amending Accessibility Code
sections.summary: Proposes amending the Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment to require at least one lactation room per 2,500 square metres in GFA in offices and business parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My first proposal is to amend the Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment to require at least one lactation room per 2,500 square metres in GFA in offices and business parks.

sections.label: WeWork lactation room booking data
sections.summary: WeWork data from January to May 2023 found over 1,300 hours of bookings for their lactation rooms, showing high demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Data from WeWork between January and May 2023 found over 1,300 hours of bookings for their lactation rooms, showing the high demand for lactation rooms.

sections.label: Second proposal mandating lactation facilities
sections.summary: Proposes mandating the facilities required in lactation rooms at workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second proposal is that we mandate the facilities required in lactation rooms at workplaces.

sections.label: Mandating lactation room items
sections.summary: Proposes mandating lactation rooms include a lockable door, mirror, wash basin with detergent and towels, hot water dispenser and waste bin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Since the Code already recognises that these facilities are important, I propose we take a small step further and mandate that lactation rooms in workplaces be not just equipped with three items but the following items as well, in order of priority: one, a door that is lockable; two, a mirror; three, a wash basin with liquid detergent and paper towels; four, a dispenser for hot water; and five, a waste bin.

sections.label: BMSG lactation room wishlist
sections.summary: BMSG has a wishlist of lactation room items: a small table, a steriliser and a dedicated refrigerator with freezer for breastfeeding mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Beyond these items, BMSG also has a wishlist of items they hope to have in a lactation room including: one, a small table; two, a steriliser; and three, a dedicated refrigerator with freezer for use by breastfeeding mothers only.

sections.label: New building standards and co-funding
sections.summary: Proposes all new buildings comply with new standards and asks MND to raise Accessibility Fund co-payment from 60% to 80% for lactation rooms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can start by making sure all new buildings comply with these new standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I also hope MND can increase the co-payment quantum in the Accessibility Fund from the current 60% to 80% for the construction of lactation rooms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We already provide the co-funding of 80% for Basic Accessibility features so why not lactation rooms too?

sections.label: Accessible toilets requirement
sections.summary: The Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment requires accessible toilets for adults with disabilities and seniors at many locations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the same Code on Accessibility in the Built Environment that I have mentioned so many times in this speech, accessible toilets for adults with disabilities and seniors must be present at a huge number of locations.

sections.label: Lactation room code reviews
sections.summary: The 2013 Code review required lactation rooms in certain building types, the 2019 review extended this, and the Accessibility Fund was enhanced in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The 2013 Code review introduced the requirement for specific building types, starting with developments, such as transport interchanges, sports complexes, community clubs and large-scale shopping centres, to provide at least one lactation room.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: After another review in 2019, this requirement was extended to more building types, including offices and business parks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We also enhanced the Accessibility Fund in 2022 to cover more buildings.

sections.label: BCA consultation timeline
sections.summary: BCA aims to commence public consultation on the enhanced Code by end 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: BCA aims to commence public consultation on the enhanced Code by end 2024.

sections.label: Accessibility Fund co-funding lactation rooms
sections.summary: The government encourages feedback and will consider raising Accessibility Fund co-funding for lactation rooms after the Code review.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: I encourage our industry stakeholders and our advocacy groups to continue providing feedback, to help us shape a more accessible and inclusive built environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We also note Mr Ng's recommendation to increase the co-funding amount under the Accessibility Fund to meet the construction cost of lactation rooms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will consider this following the completion of the Code review.

sections.label: Employer breastfeeding support practices
sections.summary: Employers are encouraged to adopt the Tripartite Standard on Work-Life Harmony and use the Employer's Guide to Breastfeeding at the Workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For example, employers are encouraged to adopt the Tripartite Standard on Work-Life Harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These include cultivating a breastfeeding-friendly culture in the workplace, offering flexible lactation breaks and providing private lactation rooms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Finance and National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will also continue promoting best practices through the Employer's Guide to Breastfeeding at the Workplace, jointly produced by the NTUC U Family, Health Promotion Board and the Singapore National Employers Federation, which includes recommendations on what employers can do to support breastfeeding employees who are returning to work.

sections.label: Request to raise co-funding now
sections.summary: Mr Ng asks that co-funding be increased to 80% now, before the Code review, to help building owners install lactation facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: From her smiles, I have a sense that maybe the recommendations will be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: But, I think she mentioned about the accessibility fund and that they are considering increasing it to 80%; but only after the Code is reviewed, which could take another year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Could I just ask that in the interim we consider increasing the co-funding to 80% now, because I know cost is a big factor for building owners; and, I think, if we increase it to 80%, there is a good chance that more of the building owners will install the lactation pods or construct a lactation room.

sections.label: Reason for waiting for Code review
sections.summary: The government says consideration after the Code review depends on what the Code proposes, recommends or mandates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The reason why we would consider this after the Code review is because much depends on what the Code proposes or recommends and what the Code mandates.

sections.label: Interim lactation pods and Accessibility Fund
sections.summary: The government notes Mr Ng's urgency concerns, saying lactation pods and the Accessibility Fund are available in the interim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But we note Mr Ng's concerns about the urgency and the need to assist them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But in the meantime, as I said, lactation pods are a good way to provide facilities in the interim and the Accessibility Fund is available for that.
